nodes.name: Lemma 5.1: Decomposition
nodes.statement:
There is an $O(nk)$ time algorithm that, given any constant-factor approximation $C^\ast$ for robust $k$-median on $X$, decomposes $X$ as
	\[
		X=F\cup R\cup G,
	\]
	where
	\begin{itemize}[itemsep=0pt,topsep=0pt]
	\item $F$ is a finite subset of $X$ with $|F| = O(m+\varepsilon^{-1})$, 
	\item $R$ is the union $R=R_1\cup\cdots\cup R_l$ with $l=O(\log (mk))$, each $R_i$ being an $(r_i,k)$-instance satisfying $\sum_{i\in [l]} r_i|R_i| = O(\cost^{(m)}(X,C^\ast))$, 
	\item $G$ is an $(r_{{\mathrm{in}}},k)$-instance, where $r_{{\mathrm{in}}} = \varepsilon/(mk)\cdot \cost^{(m)}(X,C^\ast)$.
	\end{itemize}

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4: Reduction to regular instances
nodes.statement:
Let $(M,\mathrm{dist})$ be a metric space with VC dimension $d_{\mathrm{VC}}$ and doubling dimension $d_D$.

Let $d = \min\{d_{\mathrm{VC}}, d_D\}$.

There is a randomized algorithm which, given an $(r,k)$-instance $X$, computes with probability at least $1- O(\frac{1}{\log (mk)})
	$  an $(\varepsilon,m,\varepsilon r |X|)$-robust coreset with size $\tilde{O}(kd\varepsilon^{-2})\cdot \log^3 m$ of $X$ for robust \textsc{$k$-Medians}\xspace.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.5: Reduction to vanilla case
nodes.statement:
Suppose there exists a randomized algorithm $\mathcal{B}$ that on every \textsc{$k$-Medians}\xspace instance, with probability at least $0.9$, computes a vanilla $\varepsilon$-coreset with size $Q(\varepsilon)$.
Given an $(r,k)$-instance $X$, with probability at least $0.9$, Algorithm~alg_coreset2 computes an $(\varepsilon,m,mkr)$-robust coreset with size $k+Q(\varepsilon)$ of $X$ for robust \textsc{$k$-Medians}\xspace.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.3: Coreset for regular instances
nodes.statement:
Let $(M,\mathrm{dist})$ be a metric space with VC dimension $d_{\mathrm{VC}}$ and doubling dimension $d_D$.

Let $d = \min\{d_{\mathrm{VC}}, d_D\}$.

Assume that $X\subseteq M$ is an $(r,k_0)$-regular instance with $|X|=n$.
With probability $1-O\big(\frac{1}{\log(k/\varepsilon)\cdot \log (mk)}\big)$, Algorithm~alg_coreset returns an $(\varepsilon,m,\varepsilon n r)$-robust coreset of $X$ for robust \textsc{$k$-Medians}\xspace with size $kd\varepsilon^{-2}\cdot \log^{O(1)}(kd\varepsilon^{-1})\cdot \log^3 m$.

nodes.name: Lemma 6.4: Sufficient conditions for coresets
nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be an $(r,k_0)$-regular instance of size $n$ and $D$ a weighted subset of $X$.
If $D$ is simultaneously capacity-respecting, an $\varepsilon$-range space approximation and an $\varepsilon$-indexed-subset cost approximation of $X$, then $D$ is an $(O(\varepsilon),m,O(\varepsilon n r ))$-robust coreset of $X$.

Lemma 6.5: Uniform sampling satisfies the conditions
nodes.statement:
With probability at least $1-O\big(\frac{1}{\log (k/\varepsilon)\cdot \log (mk)}\big)$,  Algorithm~alg_coreset outputs a weighted set $D$ which
is simultaneously an $\varepsilon$-range space approximation of $X$, an $\varepsilon$-indexed-subset cost approximation of $X$ and capacity-respecting with respect to $X$.
